title: Trapping Rain Water

content.problemStatement: Given an array of non-negative integers representing elevation heights where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
content.inputFormat:
First line: Integer n

Second line: n space-separated integers
content.outputFormat: Print a single integer — total trapped water.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Example demonstrating Two-pointer approach tracking max_left and max_right boundaries to accumulate trapped rainwater in O(N).

solution.approach: Two-pointer approach tracking max_left and max_right boundaries to accumulate trapped rainwater in O(N).

code.Python3:
import sys
def main():
    toks = [int(x) for x in sys.stdin.read().split()]
    if toks:
        n = toks[0]
        h = toks[1:1+n]
        if n <= 2: print(0); return
        l, r = 0, n - 1
        max_l, max_r = h[l], h[r]
        water = 0
        while l < r:
            if max_l <= max_r:
                l += 1
                max_l = max(max_l, h[l])
                water += max_l - h[l]
            else:
                r -= 1
                max_r = max(max_r, h[r])
                water += max_r - h[r]
        print(water)
if __name__ == "__main__": main()

editorial.overview: Maintain two pointers l and r. Track max_left and max_right. Increment water trapped at current lower side.
editorial.approach: Two-pointer approach tracking max_left and max_right boundaries to accumulate trapped rainwater in O(N).

hints: Trapped water at i is min(max_left, max_right) - height[i].
